crm_notes: Background: SI-focused consultancy building a managed LLM inference stack for a large retail customer. Heavy focus on predictable throughput for peak sale events.
Initial ask: dedicated GPU pool for 24/7 baseline plus burst capacity for 48-hour sale windows. Need throughput guarantees and explicit fallbacks.

Workshop plan agreed: 2-day onsite (remote option) dedicated capacity sizing workshop with SE + infra leads. Deliverables: QPS baseline, tokens/sec profile, peak vs steady-state sizing, cost model, recommended GPU types and quantization profile.

POC scope: 1-week pilot on 8x A10G equivalent (reserved) to validate latency SLOs at 95th pct. Target: 200 qps chat baseline (avg 120 tokens/resp) with 50 qps burst to 700 qps during peak using autoscale/burst policy.

Latency SLOs discussed: 95th <= 250ms for short-chat (<=256 tokens), p50 <= 80ms; long generation SLOs negotiated: p95 <= 1200ms for 1024 tokens. Redwood asked for explicit SLAs and penalty tiers; customer pushed back on strict fines — prefers credits model.
Routing/fallback strategy: prefer regional routing (NA-primary, EU backup) + model fallbacks to smaller quantized variants under overload. Must preserve deterministic outputs for reranking workloads.
Security: SAML SSO, tenant-level audit logs with 12-month retention, KMS integration for keys, optional HSM for root keys. Air-gapped option flagged for specific retail partner (legal).

Cost sensitivity: mid-high; CFO requires three options: conservative (no burst), balanced (moderate burst), aggressive (high burst, higher ARR). Engineer's ask: explicit token/sec measurements from Redwood Optimize run on sample traces.
